title: Magnetic ground state screening
action: Perform spin-polarized DFT+U total energy calculations for the four magnetic configurations (FM, A-AFM, C-AFM, G-AFM) of the bulk GBCO unit cell to confirm that G-AFM is the most stable. Record total energies for each configuration.
description: Intermediate step to establish the magnetic ground state. The agent must compute total energies and identify G-AFM as the lowest energy state.

title: Bulk geometry optimization and electronic structure
action: Using the G-AFM magnetic ordering, optimize the lattice parameters of the orthorhombic bulk GBCO unit cell and compute Co magnetic moments, Bader charges, and the band gap (from GGA+U electronic structure). Output all results in bulk_properties.json.
description: Scored step reproducing lattice constants, magnetic moments, Bader charges, and the band gap of the bulk material.
output_schema: {"lattice_constants": {"a": float, "b": float, "c": float, "volume": float}, "co_magnetic_moments": [{"label": "Co1_octa", "moment_muB": float}, {"label": "Co2_octa", "moment_muB": float}, {"label": "Co1_pyr", "moment_muB": float}, {"label": "Co2_pyr", "moment_muB": float}], "co_bader_charges": [{"label": "Co1_octa", "charge_e": float}, {"label": "Co2_octa", "charge_e": float}, {"label": "Co1_pyr", "charge_e": float}, {"label": "Co2_pyr", "charge_e": float}], "band_gap_GGA+U": float}

title: O2 molecule reference optimization
action: Optimize an isolated O2 molecule in a large supercell (e.g., 8×8×8 Å³) using spin-polarized DFT to obtain its total energy and equilibrium bond length. Record the total energy and bond length.
description: Reference calculation needed for adsorption energy definitions. The optimal O2 energy and bond length are used in subsequent steps.

title: Oxygen vacancy formation energies
action: For each distinct oxygen site in the bulk supercell (O1...O5), remove one oxygen atom to create a vacancy, relax the defective supercell, and compute the formation energy using E_f = E(def) + 0.5*E(O2) – E(perf). Output all formation energies in vacancy_formation_energies.csv.
description: Scored step reporting formation energies of oxygen vacancies at different layers.
output_schema: CSV with columns: site (string, e.g., O1, O2, O3, O4, O5), formation_energy_eV (float).

title: Perfect BaO-terminated (001) slab relaxation
action: Construct a 6-plane BaO-terminated (001) slab with a P(1×2) supercell from the relaxed bulk structure, and perform a full geometry relaxation to obtain the clean perfect surface energy and structure.
description: Intermediate step needed before O2 adsorption on the perfect surface. The relaxed slab coordinates and total energy are used in the next step.

title: O2 adsorption on perfect GBCO (001) surface
action: Place an O2 molecule at 0.25 ML coverage on the relaxed perfect slab at three adsorption sites (Ba, Bridge, O). For each, relax the geometry and compute the adsorption energy (E_ads = E(slab+O2) – E(slab) – E(O2)), Bader charges on the two O atoms and selected surface ions (Ba*, O*, sub-surface Co), and the O–O bond length. Output all results in perfect_adsorption_properties.csv.
description: Scored step providing adsorption energies, Bader charges, and bond lengths for the perfect surface. This step depends on the correct relaxed slab and O2 reference energy, making it a load-bearing scored artifact.
output_schema: CSV with columns: adsorption_site (Ba, Bridge, O), E_ads_eV, charge_Oa_e, charge_Ob_e, charge_Ba_star_e, charge_O_star_e, charge_Co_e, Oa_Ob_bond_length_A. Each row corresponds to one site.

title: Defective BaO-terminated (001) slab relaxation
action: Create a defective surface model by removing a surface oxygen atom from the perfect slab (creating a 12.5% defect concentration), and fully relax the slab.
description: Intermediate step needed before O2 adsorption on the defective surface.

title: O2 adsorption on defective GBCO (001) surface
action: Place an O2 molecule at 0.25 ML coverage on the relaxed defective slab at the same three adsorption sites (Ba, Bridge, O). For each, relax and compute the adsorption energy, Bader charges on Oa/Ob, Ba*, O*, Co, the O–O bond length, and the Oa–vacancy distance. Output all results in defective_adsorption_properties.csv.
description: Scored step for the defective surface, covering adsorption energies and structural parameters.
output_schema: CSV with columns: adsorption_site (Ba, Bridge, O), E_ads_eV, charge_Oa_e, charge_Ob_e, charge_Ba_star_e, charge_O_star_e, charge_Co_e, Oa_Ob_bond_length_A, Oa_vacancy_distance_A.
